title: Databricks lakehouse and machine learning
summary: From wind turbine readings to a model in production: SparkLab notebooks, a Databricks job under Unity Catalog, MLflow training and retries.
story: Contoso Energy runs a wind farm. The turbines' readings (`source.turbine_readings`) land in the lakehouse; the data science team wants a model that predicts the power produced from the wind, and predictions refreshed every day.

You set up the lakehouse, explore the readings, build the features in a Databricks job that runs as a service principal with least privileges, train and promote the model with MLflow, then make the job resilient to transient failures.

Nothing connects to Azure Databricks: jobs, compute, Unity Catalog and MLflow are simulated on your machine; notebooks run on SparkLab (never executed as Python) and really write to the local catalog.
goals: Understand the medallion architecture of a local lakehouse
Explore data with the SparkLab DataFrame API
Run a Databricks job as a service principal with least-privilege Unity Catalog grants
Train, register and promote a model with MLflow and an alias
Make a job resilient with retries, and read its cost

steps.title: Run the medallion lakehouse
instructions: Before the turbines, get to know the local lakehouse with the retail demo.

In **Cloud Lab › Lakehouse and notebooks**, click **Create / repair demo files**, start the runtime, then **Run local medallion flow**. The CSV goes to bronze, silver, then gold (`gold.customer_revenue`) with Polars and DuckDB, for real.
Look at the layers produced: this is the same bronze / silver / gold organization as in Databricks.

checks.label: The medallion flow ran on the local lakehouse

steps.title: Explore the readings in SparkLab
instructions: Open `projects/databricks-ml/explore_turbines.py`. Add a `wind_band` column (`low` under 8 m/s, `medium` under 14 m/s, otherwise `high`) with `F.when(...).otherwise(...)`, then aggregate by `wind_band`: `readings` (number of readings) and `avg_power` (average power).
Click **Run active SparkLab file**. The result is computed locally; the plan and the costs are simulated.

checks.label: A SparkLab run returns wind_band, readings and avg_power

steps.title: Build the features as a service principal
instructions: The `turbine_features` job (`factory/databricks/jobs/turbine_features.json`) runs as the service principal `sp-feature-eng`.

1. Complete the notebook `factory/databricks/Shared/features/nb_turbine_features.py`: keep the readings with a positive wind speed, add `power_per_wind` (power divided by wind speed) and `wind_band` (same thresholds as in SparkLab).
2. In **Cloud Lab › Databricks**, choose `turbine_features`, then **Run now**. The run fails: `sp-feature-eng` has no privileges (Unity Catalog).

3. Add the **least** privileges at the end of `factory/databricks/grants.sql`: `USE SCHEMA` on `main.source` and `SELECT` on the single table `main.source.turbine_readings`, then `USE SCHEMA` and `CREATE TABLE` on `main.silver`.
4. **Run now** again: the run succeeds and `main.silver.turbine_features` is owned by `sp-feature-eng`.
The orchestration and Unity Catalog are simulated; the notebook runs on SparkLab and really writes the table.

checks.label: A local run of turbine_features succeeded as sp-feature-eng
silver.turbine_features has the power_per_wind and wind_band columns
18 readings split into 4 low, 6 medium and 8 high, with a correct power_per_wind
checks.sql: SELECT wind_band, COUNT(*) AS readings, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ABS(power_per_wind * wind_speed - actual_power) > 0.000001) AS wrong_ratio FROM silver.turbine_features GROUP BY wind_band

steps.title: Practice: least privileges for a job
instructions: Do the exercise **Least privileges for a job's service principal**: give a service principal exactly the Unity Catalog privileges its job needs, no more, no less.

steps.title: Train and promote the model with MLflow
instructions: The `power_model_training` job trains a linear regression (power from wind speed), tracks it in MLflow, registers it in Unity Catalog as `main.ml.power_model`, gives it the `champion` alias when its error is low enough, then scores every turbine with the `champion` version.
1. In **Cloud Lab › Databricks**, choose `power_model_training`, then **Run now**. Open **Experiments and models**: version 1, alias `champion`.
2. Run the job again: version 2 is registered and the alias moves to it. The scoring loads `models:/main.ml.power_model@champion`: its code did not change.
MLflow and the registry are simulated and kept locally; the training is a real computation (least squares) on the lab rows.

checks.label: A local run of power_model_training trained, promoted and scored
main.ml.power_model has at least 2 versions and a champion alias

steps.title: Practice: track a training run with MLflow
instructions: Do the exercise **Track a training run with MLflow**: a named run, its parameters, its metric and the logged model.

steps.title: Survive transient failures
instructions: At night the cluster sometimes loses a node and the `build_features` task fails once. Add to that task, in `factory/databricks/jobs/turbine_features.json`:
"max_retries": 2,
"min_retry_interval_millis": 60000

In **Cloud Lab › Databricks**, choose `turbine_features`, set `build_features` to **fails attempt 1**, then **Run now**. The run succeeds on the second attempt; also look at what the failed attempt costs in lab DBUs.

checks.label: turbine_features succeeded after at least two attempts of build_features

steps.title: Practice: retries and a timeout
instructions: Do the exercise **Retry transient failures, not slow runs**: retries for transient failures, a timeout for stuck runs.

steps.title: Check the predictions with Polars
instructions: Optional step: it runs **real local Python**. Only enable it if you trust the code: in **Mosaic**, **Enable trusted local Python…** (the runtime restarts).

Open `projects/databricks-ml/residuals.py`, compute the absolute error of each prediction, then per turbine `readings` and `max_abs_error`, and publish the result to `metrics.turbine_residuals` with `publish(...)`. Click **Run active Python**.

checks.label: A local Python run returns turbine_id, readings and max_abs_error

steps.title: Review compute, privileges and cost
instructions: In **Cloud Lab › Databricks**, review the compute and cost of your runs, the Unity Catalog privileges and the MLflow registry, then answer the questions in `projects/databricks-ml/NOTES.md`.
This step cannot be checked automatically: tick it yourself when your notes are written.
